blocking_issues.missing_fact: For the expressed Phaffia rhodozyma CrtI, identify an independently supported terminal electron acceptor, its reduction product, and an accessible host compartment.
blocking_issues.evidence: The actual donor is fungal, not Pantoea. No primary-evidence-backed terminal acceptor/product pair was established for that fungal enzyme in this curation. Inspected Phaffia CrtI UniProt entries are unreviewed and their NAD(+) annotation is automated ARBA evidence, not a measured reaction. The identified primary fungal CrtI paper was inaccessible at the publisher. The bacterial Schaub study is not transferable proof and, even for that enzyme, does not establish released water or peroxide stoichiometry.
blocking_issues.consequence: No task_desaturation stoichiometry is supplied. Do not substitute NAD(+), oxygen-to-water, oxygen-to-peroxide, superoxide release, freely exchanging FAD/FADH2, or mitochondrial quinone reduction merely to close the equations.

blocking_issues.missing_fact: Exact engineered CrtI sequence/accession and compartment compatibility, plus an explicit interpretation of a lycopene intermediate-capacity task in strains that retain downstream CrtYB cyclase activity.
blocking_issues.evidence: The now-available condition records identify Phaffia CrtE/CrtYB/CrtI. This was independently verified against Methods 2.1.1 and the original construction Table 1. Reviewed Phaffia CrtYB Q7Z859 has both phytoene synthase and lycopene beta-cyclase activities.
blocking_issues.consequence: Do not relabel CrtYB as a standalone CrtB, assert a terminal lycopene-only construct, infer enzyme abundance from gene copies, or assume mitochondrial Q6 access. A possible upper bound on an intermediate is not a realized-content prediction.

native_host.identifier_mapping: COBRApy decodes the SBML __91__ and __93__ bracket escapes; the usable host IDs below were obtained from the loaded model, not guessed from names.
native_host.charge_limitation: The inspected SBML species omit fbc:charge. COBRApy imports their charge as 0. This is not evidence that phosphorylated metabolites or the proton are chemically neutral. Native formulas retain the protonation states; independent formal charges are checked separately for the supported precursor reactions.

existing_precursor_synthesis.protein_identity: UniProtKB Q12051, BTS1, whose reviewed catalytic annotation includes RHEA:17653 / EC 2.5.1.29 and the all-trans GGPP product.
existing_precursor_synthesis.curation_decision: Host already supplies cytosolic GGPP through a native enzyme-constrained reaction. The independently verified Phaffia CrtE constructs justify a separate heterologous extension in principle, not as a capacity convenience. Without heterologous enzyme constraints it would provide only an upper-bound bypass of native BTS1 enzyme limits. The displayed protein coefficient is existing native stoichiometry, not a newly supplied kinetic parameter.

preexisting_balance_caveat.note: A second native GGPP-neighbor reaction has this pre-existing formula imbalance. It was not changed. No full-host balance or thermodynamic validation is claimed.

supported_precursor_reaction_definitions.inclusion_status: The actual Phaffia CrtE constructs support a distinct heterologous extension in principle. No fungal enzyme capacity or gene-dose scaling is supplied.

supported_precursor_reaction_definitions.source: IUBMB EC 2.5.1.32; reviewed Phaffia CrtYB Q7Z859 / RHEA:34475 with experimental provenance PMID:10589832; actual CrtYB construct confirmed in Methods 2.1.1 and original Table 1
supported_precursor_reaction_definitions.inclusion_status: Supported as the phytoene-synthase activity of the bifunctional fungal CrtYB, not a standalone bacterial CrtB. Its downstream cyclase activity remains relevant to interpretation of the lycopene intermediate.
supported_precursor_reaction_definitions.proton_note: Two host GGPP molecules supply H66; C40H64 plus two host HO7P2 molecules also supplies H66. No H+ is added. Independent formal charges are -6 on each side.

desaturation_evidence.necessary_chemical_change_to_requested_o: C40H64 to C40H56 entails removal of eight hydrogen atoms. This arithmetic does not identify the electron acceptor or establish exclusive product specificity of the actual fungal enzyme.
desaturation_evidence.equation_limitation: The registry leaves the acceptor generic. A/AH2 is not a chemically specified metabolite pair and cannot be installed under the frozen interface's formula/charge rules.
desaturation_evidence.fungal_primary_reference_status: Verdoes, Misawa and van Ooyen (1999), PMID:10397832, was identified by metadata only. A bounded publisher full-text availability request returned HTTP 403. No fungal terminal-acceptor/product stoichiometry was thereby verified.
desaturation_evidence.unreviewed_fungal_annotation_status: O13506 and other inspected Phaffia CrtI entries carry an automated NAD(+) cofactor annotation (ECO:0000256, ARBA00001911), without a measured catalytic equation. Automated alternative naming also refers to a five-step enzyme. Neither annotation was elevated to experimental evidence or used to select a redox reaction.
desaturation_evidence.comparison_scope: Pantoea bacterial enzyme only; not evidence that the expressed fungal CrtI uses the same redox chemistry.

s4e: Desaturation Reactions in the Presence of Alternative Electron Acceptors
s4b: CRTI Cloning, Expression and Purification
comparison_evidence_statements: The purified bacterial reference CRTI requires FAD and is inactive in desaturation under nitrogen without an alternative acceptor; the authors identify oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor.

The authors report no effect of added superoxide dismutase or catalase on oxygen-consumption kinetics. They hypothesize that possible superoxide might not be released and could react with liposomal components. This does not identify a released water, peroxide, or superoxide stoichiometry.

Anaerobic liposome assays support alternative quinones, including coenzyme Q10 and duroquinone; these experiments do not specifically establish Q6 as an in vivo acceptor in the fungal yeast construct.
The discussion raises, rather than resolves, possible coupling of bacterial CRTI to a respiratory chain.

The authors conclude that reduced FAD is not exchanged with external oxidized FAD on the catalytic-cycle timescale. A net free-FAD reduction reaction is therefore not an evidence-backed substitute even for that bacterial enzyme.

cofactor_and_constraint_policy.scope_if_unblocked: upper_bound_only; feasible capacity, not realized allocation or product performance
notes: No independently transferable in vivo abundances or construct-specific kinetic constraints were established. No kcat, expression level, enzyme allocation fraction, or fitted product constant was invented.

The bacterial P21683 cofactor annotation cites ATP as required but not apparently hydrolyzed, and divalent metals; this was not transferred as a measured cofactor requirement of fungal CrtYB. No net ATP hydrolysis or construct-specific capacity was invented.

Catalytic FAD was established only for the bacterial comparator, not for the actual fungal construct by the inspected evidence. No free FAD or automatically annotated NAD(+) was used as an unverified electron sink.

Any eventual task must retain upstream host carbon, ATP and reducing-equivalent demands and the actual terminal electron-acceptor costs. No free-carbon feed, naked flux floor, artificial acceptor source, transport shortcut, or added detoxification shortcut is authorized.
All prospective new IDs are opaque; biological identities are documentary evidence, not identifiers used to trigger special model behavior.

thermodynamic_and_localization_limits: Forward-only reactions would be a pathway-direction assumption; no reaction Gibbs energies or metabolite activities were established.

An eventual cytosolic task would aggregate membrane-associated substrates into the host cytoplasmic pool. This requires compatibility with the actual targeting/localization construct, not merely an enzyme name.
Do not connect a cytosolic desaturase directly to the mitochondrial Q6 pool without independent localization or electron-transfer evidence.
Mass/charge balance does not establish thermodynamic feasibility, sufficient enzyme activity, membrane binding, realized allocation, or secretion.

parent_actions: Do not join or score a complete chemistry task from this evidence file. There is no ready chemistry.json.

Use the verified fungal CrtE/CrtYB/CrtI construct, not bacterial CrtE/CrtB/CrtI. Confirm the exact engineered CrtI accession/sequence and any localization information not given by the inspected construct descriptions.

Resolve the fungal terminal electron acceptor, reduction product, and accessible compartment from independent reaction/enzymology evidence. The identified primary fungal CrtI paper is an access-limited follow-up, not an already verified source. If chemistry remains ambiguous, retain blocked status rather than choosing a capacity-favorable route.
Account explicitly for the CrtYB cyclase and the intermediate nature of the lycopene endpoint. Do not infer gene-copy-to-activity scaling or force a downstream flux floor.

Only then create a complete schema-version-1 ChemicalTask using opaque IDs, empty enzymes unless independent compatible constraints are supplied, and explicit mass/charge-balanced physical costs. Re-run non-optimizing installation validation.
